title: sdks: unify auth/retries + streaming parity across python/ts/go and bump v1.94.0
author: Ava Chen
description: Context: We've had several drift issues between the Python, TypeScript and Go SDKs around auth token refresh semantics, retry/backoff defaults, and streaming ergonomics. This PR unifies the behaviors: - standardizes bearer token refresh hooks and automatic retry on 401 with single configurable hook; - aligns retry policy default (exponential backoff with jitter, 5 attempts) across SDKs; - improves streaming API ergonomics (context manager + async iterator parity where applicable) and fixes edge cases around partial-body errors; - bumps package versions to v1.94.0 and updates changelogs. Motivation: reduce operational surprises for customers using multi-language stacks and make rollout of auth/retry tuning consistent. Checklist: - [x] Implement unified auth hook (python/typescript/go) - [x] Centralize retry config and expose SDK-level default - [x] Streaming ergonomics: add context-manager helpers in python, unify readable stream interface in TS, stabilize Go client chunking - [x] Add E2E tests and unit tests - [x] Bump versions and changelogs - [x] Update docs and migration notes Related: Linear ENG-4821, ENG-4928; this also closes support ticket SUP-1284. Testing notes: Local e2e harness ran against mock server with token expiry simulated; CI runs include sdk-unit, integration (playground), flake8/black/lint, typecheck. Known limitations: Go still lacks Python-style context-manager pattern due to language differences (we expose Close helper and a streaming channel helper), documented in migration notes.
commits:
- 0a9b3e1: core: add unified AuthHook interface and token refresh helper across sdks
- 1c2d4f5: python: implement contextmanager for streaming and retry wrapper with backoff
- 2a7f9b2: typescript: add async iterable streaming helper + retry policy consolidation
- 3d4e5a6: go: add streaming channel helper, centralize retry backoff config
- 7f8e9d0: ci: add e2e matrix for sdk versions and token expiry simulation
- 9b0c1d2: docs: migration notes + changelogs + version bump to v1.94.0
review_comments: Diego Morales: Left a couple small nits in python streaming helper (contextmanager naming + docs) — please address.
Ava Chen: Fixed the naming nit and updated docstring examples; added additional unit test for stream close race.
Priya Shah: Verified retry defaults in TS. One request: make backoff max_delay configurable via client opts.
release_notes:
- SDKs: unify auth token refresh hook and retry/backoff defaults across Python/TS/Go
- Streaming: improved ergonomics and parity; Python adds context-manager helper, TS adds async-iterable helper, Go exposes channel-based helper
- Version bumps to v1.94.0 for all SDKs
- Docs: migration guide for auth/retry changes
notes: This PR was coordinated across language leads. Backward compatibility: existing client configs continue to work, but teams on custom retry/backoff must verify behavior due to default change. Ops: rollout monitored with canary tokens in production for 48 hours post-merge.
ci_details: CI matrix: python 3.9-3.11, node 16-20, go 1.20-1.22. Checks: sdk-unit (pass), integration-e2e (pass), lint/format (pass), typecheck (pass), security-scan (pass). One flaky test in integration for TS streaming retried and passed.
testing_summary: Added new unit tests covering token refresh on 401, retry jitter/backoff, and streaming partial-body recovery. E2E simulated token expiry and verified automatic refresh and retry; metrics show ~0.3% additional latency when refresh triggered.
